summary: A dense Vital Lacerda worker-placement game where you run an art gallery: acquiring artists and artwork, hosting exhibitions, managing an auction house, and building your reputation to draw wealthy visitors. It's a long, intricate puzzle of interlocking systems where every action ripples through several tracks at once.
praised: remarkable thematic integration of mechanisms with the art-dealing theme
high production values and clever board design
criticised: very long playtime and steep learning curve
heavy rules overhead and fiddly bookkeeping
downtime between turns at higher player counts
can feel more like solving a puzzle than competing with people

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking and competitive auctions
interaction.detail: Players place workers on a shared board of galleries, artists, and transport routes, so taking a spot or artist denies it to opponents, and the auction mechanism pits players directly against each other's bids. Each player still runs their own gallery and finances mostly independently between these contested moments.

scoring.why: Final score combines money, reputation track position, exhibition and contract bonuses, so building the strongest overall economy matters more than any single track.
scoring.how_you_win: You cultivate artists, sell and exhibit their art profitably, and climb the reputation track faster than your rivals, converting a well-run gallery into the highest end-game score.
